cards.design_implication: When modeling convective boundaries in stellar evolution simulations, one may configure the code to iteratively expand convection regions until ∇rad = ∇ad is satisfied on the convective side to ensure physical consistency.
does_not_establish: Causal conclusions in real-world stellar observations
cards.evidence_excerpt: In the new scheme, the extent of a convection region is allowed to expand at each time step until the boundaries reach the point where $ { \nabla _ { \mathrm { { r a d } } } } = { \nabla _ { \mathrm { { a d } } } }$ on their convective side.
limitations: The text notes this approach presumes mixing-driven expansion is rapid enough to be approximated as instantaneous.
The scheme does not specify the physical nature of gentle mixing beyond convective boundaries.
cards.statement: The MESA predictive mixing scheme allows the extent of a convection region to expand at each time step until the boundaries reach the point where the radiative gradient equals the adiabatic gradient on the convective side.
